summary: New sense 1: lecken lassen (Tiere; Salz)

rationale: Fills I Preterit from four after round 1 to five; explicit tongue instrument and source body parts, with plural agent assimilation. English is the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; meaning is established from the Turoyo.

summary: III kmalṭəʕənne adds a human causer and animal causee to the I animal-licking event; salt is recoverable as the licked theme. The evidence supports a new stem and Infectum, not a complete invented paradigm.
I Preterit has an l-coded agent and an unmarked theme; Infectum has subject agreement and may have a patient suffix (kluṭʕila) or omit the food object. PrS 75/8 and 82/6 document second-person forms.
Snake tongue behaviour at Lahdo The snake/3 is genuinely ambiguous. Preserve the edition’s licking wording; do not silently zoologise it as flicking or propose a technical sense.
Initial lo- in loṭaʕno at 96/151 belongs to the stem, not to negation. Negative attempted licking in PrS 82/9 concerns success in obtaining food, not a different lexical meaning.
Both input occurrences belong to the same sentence; one retained example covers the two tokens without duplication.
Lṭəʕʕe is an agent-indexed plural Preterit with assimilation, not a Detransitive. b lišonayye marks the instrument and repeated m- phrases the removal source; ḥalawe is the licked theme.
The Jan passage adds no support for or change to round-1 III lecken lassen. Its human agents and famine setting do not justify another sense or idiom.
Confirm the unattested III Preterit base and whether the causee suffix at JTM 1.1/95 is regular for the local dialect.
Does kluṭʕo lәšona mean licking the tongue or protruding/flicking it? The supplied verse and translation do not decide.
Provide a PrS page/line concordance before altering the inherited prs 208/25 and 217/35 references; PrS 72/98 is clearly the same shepherd-face example.
Does m qarʕe in this passage denote the forehead or the head more generally? The supplied machine “forehead” is retained as such, not silently substituted.
Licked themes include salt, faces, a foal, porridge, attempted chickpeas and blood. These are ordinary participant changes, without a new sense for grooming or feeding.
Humans licking food from a face supports the ordinary licking meaning already extended to food and faces in round 1. Hunger supplies the motivation, not a new lexical sense.
